newsitem.title: UK: 1996 aluminium consumption growth modest - EIU.
newsitem.headline: 1996 aluminium consumption growth modest - EIU.

text.p: World primary aluminium consumption growth will rise just two percent in 1996, against 3.4 percent in 1995, according to the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU).
In the latest edition of its World Commodity Profiles it attributed the lower growth rate to weakness of demand in the U.S. and Germany.
But with economic growth strengthening in several western economies, demand will accelerate in 1997 to 3.6 percent and increase again in 1998, the EIU said.
Apart from a recovery in major western economies, future aluminium consumption growth will be boosted by the Soviet Union and strong expansion in China and elsewhere in south-east Asia.

The end of the output-curtailing Memorandum of Understanding agreement among major producing nations coupled with the commissioning of new capacity has seen world production rise by 6.8 percent in 1996 which has, in turn, seen stocks rise.
Both these trends were seen continuing for the next two years, the EIU said.
It also saw a continued fall in aluminium prices in real terms through to 1998 offering little incentive to investors in new capacity, resulting in potential shortages beyond that date.
